title: Prepare a pain-care conversation around sustainable participation

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Preparing a care conversation is different from approving an activity or changing treatment. A peer’s confidence cannot replace individualized guidance; existing guidance also has a defined scope.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional guidance card: the person has an existing clinician-agreed option to join an ordinary seated conversation for up to the duration already specified in their private plan, with the plan’s stop/contact instructions unchanged. The card intentionally does not disclose that duration. A new standing event is not covered. The person wants to ask whether any suitable adaptation exists and how to review concerns; no actual clinical answer is supplied.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Write an agenda about the valued participation, the uncovered standing demand, access and follow-up. Mark which decisions need the care team rather than filling the missing private details.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A peer recommends doubling an activity because the first attempt seemed fine. Does this lesson authorize that change?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: The agenda can request clarification without approving the new event or inventing minutes. Later fiction: the clinic acknowledges the question; no plan change exists. Partial: a good question but an assumed trial before reply. Incorrect: use a peer’s “it is safe” as clearance or change medication. A real existing-guidance trial must follow that actual guidance, not this fictional card.
criteria: An agenda is not clinical approval
Existing guidance is not extended beyond its scope
Unknowns are not replaced by invented prescriptions

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Immediate tolerance and peer reassurance do not supply an individualized progression decision. Keep existing guidance and bring the question to the appropriate qualified route.
